53899.title: Support PLE-Offload for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
53899.body:
**⚠️  This PR is temporarily paused for maintenance. Future development will prioritize the implementation of UVA PLE-Offload #54371**.

## Purpose
support https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

## How to run

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
          --served-model-name qwen3.8-flash-next
          -tp 4
          --enable-prefix-caching
          --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'
```
Enable PLE offload:
```
VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=1
```

## Validation
- Without offload:
  - Weight formats: BF16, FP8, and NVFP4
  - Platforms: GB300, GB200, H200, and MI355X (BF16 only)
  - Parallel configurations: TP2, TP4
 
- With N-gram embedding offload:
  - Weight formats: BF16 and FP8 (NVFP4 is not currently supported)
  - Platform: GB200
  - Parallel configurations: TP2, TP4, and DP4+EP4

The validation results were provided by Inferact. See the [vLLM recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) for details. 

> PLE-Offload with direct UVA table lookup is being implemented in  PR #54371.

57562.title: [Bug]: AsyncScheduler num_output_placeholders underflow with chunked prefill + concurrency (no spec decode, no preemption) — regression from 0.24.0
57562.body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM **0.29.0** (official `vllm-0.29.0+cu129` wheel, and also reproduced with the CUDA 13.0 wheel)
- torch 2.13.0, transformers 5.15.0, flashinfer 0.6.18, triton 3.7.1
- Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` (hybrid Gated DeltaNet + attention, MoE 35B total / 3B active)
- GPU: 1× H100 NVL (SM90), no MIG, no tensor/pipeline parallelism
- **No speculative decoding** (`speculative_config=None`)
- Async scheduling: enabled (the 0.29.0 default)
- Chunked prefill enabled, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, `max_model_len=262144`, `max_num_seqs=64`
- Prefix caching enabled (also reproduced with it disabled)

Selected backends at startup: `FLASH_ATTN` attention, `TRITON` Fp8 MoE, `GDN decode kernel: cuda`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`EngineCore` dies with

```
File "vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 724, in step_with_batch_queue
    engine_core_outputs = self.scheduler.update_from_output(
File "vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", line 1957, in update_from_output
    new_token_ids, stopped = self._update_request_with_output(
File "vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py", line 63, in _update_request_with_output
    assert request.num_output_placeholders >= 0
AssertionError
```

**The trigger is chunked prefill concurrent with other requests generating.** No speculative decoding, no preemption, no `/v1/realtime` streaming input.

#### What the counters say at the moment of underflow

I patched in a log line at the assert and clamped to 0 instead of dying, so I could collect many samples in one run. All 44 occurrences in a 12-request load had the same signature:

```
UNDERFLOW req=... placeholders=-1 new_tokens=1 computed=8448 num_tokens=9119 prompt=9118
          output=1 in_flight=1056 stale=0 drop_stale=False prefill_chunk=True
          status=RUNNING preemptions=0 spec=0
```

`num_computed_tokens (8448) < num_tokens (9119)` — the prompt has not finished prefilling — yet **the model runner returned a sampled token for that step**. `discard_request_mask` should have suppressed it (`optimistic_seq_len < num_tokens`). The scheduler correctly classified the step as a prefill chunk (`prefill_chunk=True`) and reserved no placeholder, so the delivery decrements below zero.

The spurious tokens are appended to the response: the same request underflows repeatedly with `output` growing 1 → 2 → … → 7 while still prefilling. **The assert appears to be protecting against silently corrupted output**, so removing it would be the wrong fix.

#### Controlled experiments

| Condition | Underflows |
|---|---|
| Prompts ≤ `max_num_batched_tokens` (single chunk), 18 requests | **0** |
| Mixed prompt lengths up to ~143k tokens (multi-chunk), 12 requests | **44** |
| One ~143k-token prompt alone, no concurrency | **0** |
| `--no-enable-prefix-caching` | still dies (same assert, same trace) |
| `--no-async-scheduling` | **24/24 requests complete, no underflow** |

Occurrence count scales with chunk count: ~143k-token prompts → 14 occurrences, ~42k → 4–5, ~9k → 1. Prompts that fit in one chunk never underflow.

#### Not fixed by #50692

I applied the one-line production change from #50692 (reserve when `num_computed_tokens < num_tokens` instead of `is_prefill_chunk`) to 0.29.0 and re-ran the same load on the same machine. **It still dies with the same assert.** That is consistent with the data above: the runner returns a token for a step where `computed < num_tokens`, so mirroring the runner's *intended* mask still under-reserves.

#### Regression: 0.24.0 does not do this

With the identical instrumentation, the identical load, and async scheduling enabled, **vLLM 0.24.0 produced 0 underflows** (and survives 48/48 requests at concurrency 12). The scheduler-side accounting is byte-identical between the versions (the `is_prefill_chunk` expression, and the `discard_request_mask` block in `gpu_model_runner.py` — I diffed them). So the divergence is on the runner side: whether a sampled token is returned during an incomplete prefill.

`vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py` is byte-identical across 0.24.0/0.25.0/0.26.0, and byte-identical across 0.27.0/0.28.0/0.29.0 (the `num_stale_output_tokens` / `is_stale` rework from #48245). I have not identified which change causes the runner to emit the token.

### 🔁 Reproduction

1. Serve a hybrid GDN model on a single H100 with the defaults (async scheduling on, chunked prefill on, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`):

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill
```

2. Send ~6 concurrent streaming chat completions whose prompts are **longer than `max_num_batched_tokens`** and of differing lengths (I used ~9k / ~42k / ~143k tokens), with differing `max_tokens`.

3. `EngineCore` dies within about a second.

Requests whose prompts fit in a single chunk do not trigger it, and a single long request with no concurrency does not trigger it.

### Workaround

`--no-async-scheduling` avoids it. In our measurements the throughput cost of disabling it was below the noise floor of our benchmark.

### Related

- #35755 / #50692 — same assert, but triggered by `/v1/realtime` streaming input. #50692's fix does not address this case (measured, see above).
- #48245 — introduced the stale-output rework present in 0.27.0+.
- #46424 — notes that Mamba/GDN attention reclassifies a single-query-token prefill as a decode step; possibly related, though that path requires speculative decoding.

53480.title: [Bug][XPU]: Silent persistent output corruption (endless "!" / token 0) under sustained concurrent decode on Arc Pro B70, W4A16 27B head_dim 256
53480.body:
## Summary

A W4A16 (compressed-tensors, group 128, symmetric) 27B Qwen-family model served on a single Intel Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage, 32GB, xe driver) intermittently degenerates into emitting only "!" tokens (token id 0) under sustained concurrent decode. The corruption is silent: HTTP 200, finish_reason length, zero dmesg events, container healthy, /v1/models fine. It is PERSISTENT: after load drops, even fresh single-request generations return only "!" until the engine is restarted. Engine restart fully recovers (weight reload), which points at long-lived VRAM state (weights or a persistent workspace) being corrupted in place.

It struck our production engine four times in ~30 hours (three times at <= 4 concurrent requests after hours of sustained load; once within ~10 minutes when 12 concurrent synthetic streams mixed with real long-prompt traffic). Two sibling W4A16 models (14B and 8B, head_dim 128) on the same silicon under continuous scoring load have never corrupted in weeks, including c=12 stress sweeps.

The everything-token-0 signature suggests logits collapsing to NaN/zero (argmax degenerates to index 0), i.e. numeric poisoning of something persistent rather than per-request state.

## Environment

- GPU: Intel Arc Pro B70 32GB (Battlemage); reproduced on TWO different physical cards (VM, VFIO passthrough), so not a single-card hardware fault
- Host: kernel 6.17.0-41-generic, xe driver
- Image: intel/vllm:0.21.0-ubuntu24.04-20260805 (vLLM 0.21.1.dev18+g8df6feb7d)
  - torch 2.11.0+xpu, triton_xpu 3.7.0, vllm_xpu_kernels 0.1.8.2, dpcpp_cpp_rt 2025.3.2
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B fine-tune, W4A16 AutoRound -> compressed-tensors (group_size 128, symmetric, no g_idx), hidden 5120, 64 layers, head_dim 256, GQA 24/4, vocab 248320, lm_head unquantized
- Serve: --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype auto --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 --max-num-seqs 4..12 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048, no prefix caching
- Startup selects XPUwNa16LinearKernel (torch.ops._xpu_C.int4_gemm_w4a16) for CompressedTensorsWNA16; FLASH_ATTN (FA2) backend

## Fastest observed onset

Ramped concurrency sweep (cover-letter-shaped requests, max_tokens 700, 150s per level, c = 1, 2, 4, 8, 12) against the production engine while real traffic (6.7k-7.8k-token prompts, 2k-token completions) was also landing:

| c  | gen tok/s | mean e2e | garbage responses |
|----|-----------|----------|-------------------|
| 1  | 11.9      | 25.2s    | 0 |
| 2  | 26.0      | 24.4s    | 0 |
| 4  | 52.6      | 22.1s    | 0 |
| 8  | 102.6     | 23.3s    | 0 |
| 12 | 167.0     | 50.3s    | 36/36 (all "!") |

After the load stopped, a single-stream probe still returned 60 tokens of "!". Zero dmesg events throughout. Restart recovered.

## Isolation runs (all CLEAN, which is what makes this hard)

Each row is a separate fresh engine on the same hardware, 4-15 minute runs:

| model | image | gpu-mem-util | workload | result |
|-------|-------|--------------|----------|--------|
| 27B | dev18 | 0.90 | cold c=12, 133 reqs | clean |
| 27B | dev17 (intel/vllm:latest, 20260625 build) | 0.90 | cold c=12, 129 reqs | clean |
| 27B | dev17 | 0.97 | cold c=12, 134 reqs | clean |
| 27B | dev17 | 0.97 | full ramp c=1..12 | clean |
| 27B | dev18 | 0.97 | full ramp c=1..12 (exact replication of the corrupting run, minus live traffic) | clean |
| 27B | dev18 | 0.97 | 10 short-decode streams + 2 long-prompt (7k-token, chunked prefill) streams, 6 min | clean |
| 14B W4A16 head_dim 128 | dev18 | 0.5 | cold c=12, 239 reqs | clean |

So no single factor (image build, gpu-memory-utilization, ramp history, or a naive mixed prefill+decode workload) deterministically reproduces it from a cold engine in minutes. Production hit it four times in 30 hours. It behaves like a race whose probability rises steeply with decode batch depth and with real-traffic batch compositions.

## What we ruled out

- Hardware: identical corruption on two different physical cards; a c=12 sweep on the second card corrupted the same way while weeks of equal-wattage load from the head_dim-128 models never did. Power delta between clean c=8 (195W) and corrupting c=12 (199W) is ~2%.
- The int4 GEMM kernel in isolation: a standalone harness driving torch.ops._xpu_C.int4_gemm_w4a16 with this model's exact layer shapes (5120x8192, 6144x5120, 5120x34816, 17408x5120, group 128) at M = 1..32, 64, 128, 512, 2048 shows no NaN/Inf, bit-exact determinism across repeated calls, no input-buffer mutation (weight/scale checksums stable), and no cross-call poisoning of a baseline M=1 result.
- vLLM Python-level differences: the dev17 and dev18 images' /opt/vllm/vllm trees are byte-identical except _version.py and an API-middleware helper; torch/triton/vllm_xpu_kernels/dpcpp versions are identical. (We initially suspected a build regression; the tree diff killed that.)
- KV preemption: vLLM logged zero preemptions in all runs (KV was never near full; 172k-token cache vs ~10-40k in flight).

## Notes that may help localize it

- head_dim 256 + GQA 24/4 is the standout difference from our never-corrupting 14B/8B (head_dim 128) neighbors; vllm_xpu_kernels 0.1.8.2 predates the v0.1.9 mixed-batch attention rework.
- vocab 248320 means the (unquantized bf16) lm_head GEMM's M equals the decode batch depth; corruption onset correlates with deeper decode batches.
- The corruption survives across requests but not restarts: whatever is poisoned lives in VRAM for the process lifetime (weights, persistent workspace, or compiled-graph buffers).
- Ubuntu 24.04 HWE-class host kernel with xe; the same box previously produced GP-fault/BCS-reset issues under TP=2 (#41663) but this failure mode has no driver-visible events at all.

## Ask

We are happy to run instrumented builds, extra logging, or targeted experiments on this hardware; the model and full configs can be shared. Detection guidance for other users: only a CONTENT probe catches this (health endpoints and /v1/models keep answering normally); we run a cron t

55533.title: [Bug][Spec Decode] Hybrid GDN (Qwen3.5/Qwen3.8 27B-class) + MTP: scheduler runs only ~3 concurrent sequences at batch >= 4 — acceptance/throughput collapse
55533.body:
### Title

[Bug][Spec Decode] Hybrid GDN (Qwen3.5/Qwen3.8 27B-class) + MTP: scheduler runs only ~3 concurrent sequences at batch >= 4 — acceptance/throughput collapse

### Summary

On a 27B Qwen3.5-family hybrid GDN model (64 layers = 48 linear-attention
GDN + 16 full attention) with MTP enabled, the v1 scheduler stops running
the full batch under speculative decoding: at batch = 8, every decode
iteration schedules exactly **3 of the 8 sequences** (per-seq dist
`[2, 2, 2]` = 1 target + 1 draft token each); the other 5 wait
indefinitely and rotate in only as earlier sequences finish. The batch
"rotates" through a ~3-wide MTP concurrency window, so mean emitted
tokens per sequence per iteration drops to 0.27-0.6 and MTP becomes 2-3x
**slower** than no-spec decoding. bs <= 3 is healthy (per-position
acceptance 0.67-0.74, +33-72% throughput).

The same harness on the 24-layer-GDN 9B sibling model schedules all
batches up to bs = 20 with MTP and shows no collapse — the cap scales
with the GDN layer count / per-sequence mamba state size, which points
at the mamba cache budget being shared between target states and MTP
draft slots in the scheduler accounting.

### Environment

- vLLM built from source at f4eccda (current main as of 2026-09-06);
  also reproduces on several builds over the past week
- torch 2.13.0+cu130, RTX 4090 D (SM89), WSL2, driver 615.65.06
- model: Qwen3.8-27B GPTQ INT4 g128 (Marlin path) — quant-path
  independent (W4A16 vs W4FP8 identical), lm_head fp8 on/off identical
- offline `LLM(...)`, `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`,
  `mamba_ssm_cache_dtype=bfloat16`, gpu_memory_utilization 0.90,
  max_model_len 4608, max_num_seqs 25, KV bf16 and fp8 both tested

### Repro

```python
llm = LLM(model=<27B hybrid GDN checkpoint>, max_model_len=4608,
          gpu_memory_utilization=0.90, max_num_seqs=25,
          mamba_ssm_cache_dtype="bfloat16",
          speculative_config={"method": "mtp",
                              "num_speculative_tokens": 1})
# 8 prompts x 256 tokens, greedy, 48 generated tokens
```

Patch `Scheduler.schedule` to log
`(total_num_scheduled_tokens, len(num_scheduled_tokens), dist)` per call
after warmup. Every decode iteration shows `total=6, dist=[2,2,2]`.

Full trace: run 8x256-token prompts, greedy 256 tokens, and record
per-iteration `emitted` — iterations average 4.95 emitted tokens for 8
active sequences (e.g. 414 iterations for 8x256 tokens).

### Observed

| bs | no-spec tok/s | MTP k=1 tok/s | mean accepted len (per seq per iter) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 56.4 | 72.0 | 0.86 |
| 3 | 150.6 | 203.7 | 0.84 |
| 4 | 195.4 | 157.8 | **-0.03** |
| 8 | 367.1 | 197.0 | **-0.38** |
| 20 | 649.0 | 210.9 | **-0.73** |

(mean accepted len < 1 means some iterations schedule a given sequence
with zero tokens; decode iterations exceed generated tokens — 962
iterations for 20x256 tokens at bs=20.)

- Correctness is preserved: greedy outputs still match the no-spec
  baseline on some legs (2/2), so this is a concurrency/scheduling
  limitation, not output corruption.
- Path-independent: identical collapse on GPTQ-Marlin W4A16 and
  W4A8-FP8 (int4 x fp8 activations), on bf16 and fp8 KV cache, with
  Triton-FLA and fused-CUDA GDN decode kernels.
- Upstream `874df93` (preserve mamba state for padded prompt tails)
  fixed exactly the bs=4 point; bs>=5 persists.

### Expected

All batch sequences are scheduled under MTP every iteration (mean
accepted length per sequence per iteration >= 1.0, as observed on the
24-GDN-layer 9B sibling model up to bs=20).

### Related but distinct

- #53051: GDN state loss when prompt length == 1 + k (shape-aliasing
  prefill dispatch) — different trigger; our repro uses 256-token
  prompts at k=1 on current main.
- #55357: episodic 0% acceptance on qwen4_exp — similar symptom,
  different model family.
- #47277 / #39680: "Qwen3.5 MTP slower than no-MTP" performance reports
  — this trace is (we believe) the mechanism at 27B scale.

### Note

The debugging data above was collected with an agent-driven harness
under human supervision; happy to run anything else needed (traces,
config variations) on the 27B checkpoint.

57680.title: [Bug]: Decode throughput drops ~3.3x from 0.26.0 to 0.29.0 on H100 (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8, same config, same backends)
57680.body:
### Your current environment

- Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` (hybrid Gated DeltaNet + attention, MoE 35B total / 3B active)
- GPU: 1× H100 NVL (SM90), no MIG, TP=1, PP=1
- No speculative decoding, no LoRA, no KV connector
- `--max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 64 --enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill --load-format safetensors`
- Confidential Computing VM (AMD SEV-SNP + H100 CC mode)

Three images differing only in the vLLM release and what it pulls in:

| | vLLM | torch | triton | CUDA toolkit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 0.24.0 | 2.11.0 | 3.6.0 | 12.9 |
| B | **0.26.0** | 2.11.0 | 3.6.0 | 13.0 |
| C | **0.29.0** | 2.13.0 | 3.7.1 | 13.0 |

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Decode throughput drops ~3.3× on 0.29.0 versus 0.26.0 on identical hardware and configuration.** 0.26.0 is slightly *faster* than 0.24.0, so this is not a gradual drift — it appears between 0.26.0 and 0.29.0.

Output 512 tokens with `ignore_eos`, ~122-token prompt, **median of 5 repetitions** (single measurements are unusable, see below):

| | c=1 | c=12 | inter-token latency |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (0.24.0) | 138.8 tok/s | 1183.3 tok/s | 7.08 ms |
| **B (0.26.0)** | **148.3 tok/s** | **1295.0 tok/s** | **6.68 ms** |
| **C (0.29.0)** | **41.4 tok/s** | **362.3 tok/s** | **23.88 ms** |

ITL is flat across prompt length, so this is decode, not prefill:

| prompt | B (0.26.0) ITL | C (0.29.0) ITL |
|---|---|---|
| ~120 tok | 6.68 ms | 23.88 ms |
| ~1.2k tok | 6.69 ms | 23.92 ms |
| ~12k tok | 6.76 ms | 23.98 ms |

The ratio is the same at c=1 (3.36×) and c=12 (3.27×), so it is not a fixed per-step host overhead being amortised by batching.

#### The time is spent waiting on the GPU, not in CPU work

torch profiler on the same decode workload (c=1, 256 tokens) on both:

| | B (0.26.0) | C (0.29.0) | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aten::copy_` total | 1.099 s (59.3% CPU) | **3.455 s (82.7%)** | **3.14×** |
| `aten::copy_` calls | 10,139 | **6,137** | **0.61×** |
| `aten::copy_` per call | 109.5 µs | **563.1 µs** | **5.14×** |
| `aten::_to_copy` per call | 425.8 µs | 2,068 µs | 4.86× |

**Call counts go down while per-call time goes up 5×.** `aten::copy_` is a synchronisation point, so the increase is GPU completion wait, not extra data movement or extra dispatch. The 3.14× seen from the CPU side matches the 3.3× decode slowdown.

#### What we ruled out (all measured)

| Hypothesis | Result |
|---|---|
| CUDA 12.9 vs 13.0 | Not it — 0.26.0 is fast on CUDA 13.0 |
| Missing tuned MoE config | Not it — both log `Using default MoE config`, same path |
| Fused GDN decode kernel | Not it — 0.26.0 does not have it at all and is faster; adding it on 0.29.0 (CUDA 13.0 build) did not help |
| Attention backend | Same (`FLASH_ATTN` on both) |
| MoE backend | Same (`TRITON` Fp8, `MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEPModular`) |
| cudagraph mode | Same (`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, captured on both) |
| torch.compile / inductor | Applied on both |
| Async scheduling | No measurable difference on/off |
| `--performance-mode throughput` (new in 0.29.0) | No measurable difference |

So the selected code paths are identical and the difference is in what those kernels cost.

#### Measurement instability is itself a symptom

On 0.29.0, c=1 alternates deterministically between **41.4 and 60.8 tok/s** (values: 41.4, 60.8, 41.4, 60.5, 41.4) — a 1.47× swing, request by request. It is not prefix caching (persists with unique prompts) and not async scheduling (persists with `--no-async-scheduling`). 0.24.0 and 0.26.0 are stable to within 1% (e.g. 1294–1296 tok/s at c=12). We have no explanation for the bimodality.

#### We cannot name the kernel

```
CUPTI_ERROR_CONFIDENTIAL_COMPUTING_NOT_SUPPORTED (41)
CUPTI initialization failed - CUDA profiler activities will be missing
```

**CUPTI does not work under Confidential Computing**, so `ProfilerActivity.CUDA` yields zero events — even for a bare 10-iteration matmul. We can only see the CPU side. If someone can reproduce this on a non-CC H100, a kernel-level trace would localise it immediately.

### Reproduction

Serve `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` on one H100 with the settings above, and measure decode throughput with a fixed 512-token `ignore_eos` completion at concurrency 1 and 12. Compare 0.26.0 against 0.29.0. **Take the median of several repetitions** — single runs on 0.29.0 land on either side of the bimodal split.

### Related

- vllm-project/vllm#57562 — the `num_output_placeholders` underflow we hit on 0.29.0 (separate issue, also a 0.24.0 → 0.29.0 regression).

40926.title: [Bug]: V1 engine + MTP + GLM-5.1 (DSA + MoE + MLA) — workers hang under sustained traffic, sample_tokens RPC timeout, EngineDeadError
40926.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Under V1 engine + MTP speculative decoding + TP=8 + GLM-5.1-FP8 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`), workers hang under sustained production traffic. The scheduler is unable to advance — `step_counter=0` in the dump, requests stuck in flight — and after 30s the `sample_tokens` RPC times out, killing EngineCore. The container's outer process survives so vLLM internally restarts the engine (~12-17 min downtime), but this is a recurring failure pattern.

This is the same bug `jsboige` diagnosed for `new-TonyWang` in [#35104](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35104#issuecomment-4308377748) — a different bug than what PR #40303 fixes (no `SystemError`, no `memory_fence` on the stack). new-TonyWang's report is buried in #35104 comments and has no standalone issue, so filing here.

### Stack trace

```
File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 1205, in _process_engine_step
    outputs, model_executed = self.step_fn()
File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 523, in step_with_batch_queue
    model_output = future.result()
...
File ".../vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 388, in get_response
    raise TimeoutError(f"RPC call to {method} timed out.") from e
TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out.
```

The underlying cause:

```
File ".../vllm/distributed/device_communicators/shm_broadcast.py", line 756, in dequeue
    with self.acquire_read(timeout, indefinite) as buf:
File ".../shm_broadcast.py", line 675, in acquire_read
    self._spin_condition.wait(timeout_ms=read_timeout.timeout_ms())
File ".../shm_broadcast.py", line 632, in timeout_ms
    raise TimeoutError
```

Workers are stuck upstream of the message queue — no output coming back. Scheduler dump confirms it:

```
SchedulerStats(num_running_reqs=2, num_waiting_reqs=0, step_counter=0,
  kv_cache_usage=0.405, prefix_cache_stats=PrefixCacheStats(reset=False, requests=0, ...),
  spec_decoding_stats=None, ...)
```

### Reproduction (deterministic given enough wall clock)

| Setup |
|---|
| Image: built from v0.20.0 tag, `--target vllm-openai`, CUDA 13.0, Py 3.12, torch 2.11 |
| Hardware: 8× NVIDIA H200 (140 GB each) |
| Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8` (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` — DeepSeek Sparse Attention + MoE + MLA) |
| TP=8, EP=true |
| KV: fp8, prefix-caching on, max-model-len 202752 |
| Speculative: `{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}` |
| Allocator: `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` + `--disable-custom-all-reduce` (required to avoid torch 2.11 fragmentation OOM at boot) |
| LMCache enabled via `kv_connector=LMCacheConnectorV1` |
| Workload: real chat-completion traffic, ~0.2 RPS sustained, prompt sizes 1k–70k tokens |

### MTTF measured

| Config | Mean Time To Failure |
|---|---|
| Baseline (above) | **~38 minutes** |
| + `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` | **~5h 12min** |
| MTP off (`speculative_config=None`) | stable indefinitely |

`--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` mitigates but does not fix. Disabling MTP entirely is the only path to stable serving.

### What we ruled out

- Not OOM: GPU memory peaked at ~133 GB (94% util) sustained without exhausting. `expandable_segments:True` resolves the torch 2.11 fragmentation regression we initially hit.
- Not the descriptor-corruption bug fixed by [#40303](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40303): no `SystemError`, `memory_fence` not on stack.
- Not specific to autotune compiling kernels mid-request: disabling autotune extends MTTF 8× but doesn't eliminate the hang.
- Not capacity-bound: only 2 in-flight requests when crash occurs, kv_cache_usage 0.40.
- Not LMCache-specific: same crash signature on Plan B v3/v4 attempts (cu130-nightly + MTP) before LMCache wheel work.

### Likely candidates for the actual root cause (per `jsboige`'s diagnosis)

1. **MTP speculative decoding deadlock** in V1 + `step_with_batch_queue` + the multi-token draft path. `scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={req: [-1, -1, ...]}` (all rejected on the failing iteration) suggests the spec decode draft itself may be the hang site.
2. **DSA (Deepseek Sparse Attention) interaction** with the MTP draft head. GLM-5.1's `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` uses DSA, and the MTP head appears to feed forward through this path.
3. Some interaction with the V1 `step_with_batch_queue` async pipeline that's specific to MoE+MLA+MTP.

### Suggested debug

Per `jsboige`'s recommended isolation in #35104:
- `py-spy dump --pid <Worker_TP0 PID>` at the moment of hang to identify which subsystem the worker is actually stuck in.
- Reduce to TP=4 to see if the hang persists (TP-related?).
- Try MTP n=1 instead of n=2 — we observed n=1 still hangs in earlier testing.

We can collect `py-spy dump` next time it occurs in our deployment if helpful. Auto-rollback fires within 2s of the log signature, so we have a narrow window.

### Cross-references
- [#35104](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35104) — `jsboige` diagnosed `new-TonyWang`'s report as this same bug (different from #35104's primary fix scope).
- [#34449](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34449) — closed; was the original GLM-5 + MTP malformed tool-calls bug, **fixed** in v0.20.0 (we confirmed: tool tests 16/16 with MTP). This issue is the *next* MTP blocker after that one.

46121.title: [Performance]: Add a model-free microbenchmark for the frontend <-> EngineCore IPC path
46121.body:
## Proposal to improve performance

To be clear, this is a benchmarking/tooling proposal, not a code optimization by itself. It adds a model-free microbenchmark that isolates the frontend to EngineCore IPC cost from model execution, so that future performance work on this path can be evaluated with numbers. It measures `MsgpackEncoder` / `MsgpackDecoder` and ZMQ multipart send/recv using the same zero-copy threshold and socket helper (`make_zmq_socket`) as the serving path, and gives reviewers a local tool for evaluating future serialization, ZMQ, `copy=False`, buffer-reuse, and Rust frontend runtime changes without relying on noisy end-to-end model benchmarks.

That IPC path runs on every online request, in both directions, and is pure CPU plus transport:

```text
API server / AsyncLLM -> MsgpackEncoder -> ZMQ multipart send -> EngineCore input thread -> MsgpackDecoder
EngineCore output thread -> MsgpackEncoder -> ZMQ multipart send -> API server / AsyncLLM -> MsgpackDecoder
```

Today there is no benchmark for this path; coverage is correctness-only (`tests/v1/test_serial_utils.py`, `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_client.py`). The script would live under `benchmarks/` as a local tool (not necessarily CI-gated): selectable `ipc` (default) / `tcp` transport, encode/decode-only and ZMQ echo round-trip modes, payload sizes straddling the 256B inline-vs-aux boundary, reporting p50/p90/p99 latency, throughput, multipart frame count, and inline-vs-aux frame counts.

I would like to work on this and send a PR with the script and a results table.

## Report of performance regression

Not a regression report.

## Misc discussion on performance

One concrete question this surfaces: `VLLM_MSGPACK_ZERO_COPY_THRESHOLD` defaults to 256 and the encoder uses `< threshold`, so a 256B payload already takes the aux-buffer multipart path. The benchmark measures the per-call cost on both sides of that boundary, which would let us revisit whether 256 is the right default.

## Your current environment

Will include CPU model, OS/kernel, Python, pyzmq, and msgspec versions with the results in the PR (this path is CPU/IPC-bound, not GPU-bound).

## Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Searched existing and past issues; no benchmark exists for this path. Related active work this would serve: #45730 (zero-copy output buffer lifetime) and #46051 (Rust frontend ZMQ runtime).

49628.title: [V1][Observability] Add opt-in diagnostics for stalled engine stages
49628.body:
## Purpose

Production engine stalls are difficult to diagnose when the EngineCore process remains alive but stops making progress. These incidents do not raise an exception, so the existing exception-triggered diagnostic path never runs. Operators may see requests hang without enough evidence to determine whether the engine is waiting on model execution, token sampling, structured output processing, or another thread.

This PR adds an opt-in, stage-aware watchdog for slow V1 engine execution. When a monitored stage exceeds the configured timeout, vLLM captures the scheduler state associated with that iteration and prints Python stack traces for all threads while the stall is still occurring.

This provides production operators with:

- The stalled stage: `execute_model_wait`, `sample_tokens`, or `sample_tokens_wait`.
- A bounded configuration and scheduler summary, including queue state and request counts.
- Up to 20 representative request samples distributed across new and cached requests.
- Request IDs for correlation, with oversized IDs bounded and accompanied by their length and SHA-256 digest.
- Relevant sampling parameters, token counts, KV-block counts, multimodal counts, and embedding shapes.
- Python stack traces for every thread, which help identify where execution stopped making progress.
- Per-watchdog, per-stage throttling so a persistent stall does not flood production logs.

Prompt text, prompt token values, generated token values, multimodal contents, and unrestricted configuration objects are intentionally not logged. The complete structured summary is capped at 32 KiB.

The feature is controlled by a dedicated environment variable:

```bash
export VLLM_ENGINE_SLOW_STAGE_DUMP_S=60
```

The diagnostic is disabled when the environment variable is unset or set to `0`. In the disabled path, no watchdog thread is started and no diagnostic snapshot is constructed.

The diagnostic path is designed to fail open:
- Failure to start the watchdog disables only the diagnostic and does not prevent EngineCore startup.
- Snapshot failures fall back to a minimal diagnostic.
- Context-generation failures are reported without interrupting request processing.
- Watchdog shutdown is bounded.
- Repeated dumps for the same stage are throttled for 300 seconds.
- Throttle state belongs to each watchdog instance, so one EngineCore does not suppress diagnostics from another EngineCore in the same process.

This extends the existing exception-only dump path to cover the distinct “alive but stuck” failure mode. I did not find another open PR implementing the same V1 slow-stage watchdog.
AI assistance was used while developing this PR. I reviewed every changed line and validated the implementation and its performance.

## Test Plan
Unit/static checks:
```bash
uv run ruff check \
  vllm/logging_utils/dump_input.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_iteration_logging.py

python -m py_compile \
  vllm/logging_utils/dump_input.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_iteration_logging.py

PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/engine/test_iteration_logging.py \
  tests/test_envs.py::test_engine_timeout_environment_variables \
  -q
```

The focused tests cover:
- Default-off and explicitly enabled environment-variable behavior.
- Watchdog startup failure and bounded shutdown.
- Arming, disarming, stale generations, re-arming, and race-sensitive wakeups.
- Every retained execution stage in normal and batch-queue paths.
- Per-watchdog and per-stage throttling.
- Snapshot failures and diagnostic-output failures.
- Bounded output, request-ID truncation, and surrogate-containing request IDs.
- Sampling fairness across new and cached requests.
- Sampling-parameter cache pruning.
- Prompt, token, and configuration sanitization.
- Real SchedulerOutput, NewRequestData, and CachedRequestData objects.
- Real VllmConfig, ModelConfig, SchedulerConfig, CacheConfig, ParallelConfig, OffloadConfig, and SpeculativeConfig field contracts, so future allowlist drift fails CI.
- Current CPU-offload reporting through OffloadConfig; the removed swap-space field is not reported.

Runtime smoke validation on an H100:
1. Start vLLM with VLLM_ENGINE_SLOW_STAGE_DUMP_S=1.
2. Inject a temporary local delay into execute_model_wait to deterministically trigger the watchdog.
3. Send an OpenAI-compatible completion request.
4. Verify that the diagnostic reports the stage, scheduler summaries, and all-thread stack traces.
5. Verify that the request still completes successfully with 200 OK.
6. Verify that another timeout for the same stage is throttled.

## Test Result
Focused validation passed:
```bash

```

{"async_scheduling": true, "enable_chunked_prefill": true,

38079.title: [RFC] Redesign enable_return_routed_experts to avoid blocking EngineCore event loop
38079.body:
## [RFC] Redesign `enable_return_routed_experts` to avoid blocking EngineCore event loop

### Summary

The current `enable_return_routed_experts` implementation uses shared memory + file locks for cross-process data transfer between Worker and Scheduler. When enabled, it introduces per-step GPU→CPU synchronization on Workers and per-completed-request blocking reads on the Scheduler's single-threaded event loop. In DP+EP setups, this causes NCCL collective timeouts. We propose a per-request opt-in model with data flowing through the existing `ModelRunnerOutput` pipeline, eliminating shared memory and file locks entirely.

### Motivation

We are using `enable_return_routed_experts` in a reinforcement learning pipeline to capture MoE routing decisions during inference, which are then replayed during training. Our setup: gpt-oss-120B, TP=8, DP=2, EP=16 across 2 nodes.

**With the flag enabled, vLLM hangs within 20–60 seconds of sustained inference.** The hang manifests as throughput dropping to 0 with requests stuck "Running", eventually triggering NCCL ALLREDUCE timeouts in the expert parallel group. With the flag disabled, the same workload runs indefinitely.

### Root cause analysis

We traced the issue through a series of diagnostic experiments, systematically disabling components to isolate the cause:

| Experiment | Worker save | Scheduler read | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline (flag=False) | off | off | **OK** — sustained throughput |
| Flag=True, all default | every step | every completed req | **HANG at ~20s** |
| save=no-op, read active | off | every completed req | **HANG at ~20s** |
| save active, read=None | every step | off | **HANG at ~60s** |
| save=off (routed_experts_initialized=False), read=None | off | off | **OK** — sustained throughput |

Both the **Worker-side write path** and the **Scheduler-side read path** independently cause hangs:

**Worker-side (every forward step when flag is on):**
1. `slot_mapping_attn[:num_tokens].cpu().numpy()` — forces CUDA stream synchronization before the forward pass
2. `save_captured_experts()` — `_device_buffer.cpu().numpy()` (GPU→CPU copy ~2MB) + `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX)` + shared memory write

These per-step GPU→CPU syncs delay Workers. Since Workers across DP ranks are coupled by EP all-to-all (NCCL), one slow Worker causes cross-node collective timeouts.

**Scheduler-side (every completed request):**
1. `_get_routed_experts()` — numpy slot_mapping computation + `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX)` + shared memory read (~2MB per request)
2. For 64 concurrent 4K-token requests completing in one iteration: ~128MB of numpy copies in the single-threaded event loop

This stalls the EngineCore event loop, delaying the next `collective_rpc` to Workers, again causing EP NCCL timeouts.

### Current architecture

```
Worker Process (per GPU):
  MoE forward → capture() writes to GPU device_buffer
  After forward → save_captured_experts():
    device_buffer.cpu().numpy()          ← GPU→CPU sync (blocks CUDA stream)
    fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX)                 ← blocking file lock
    shm[slot_indices] = data             ← write to shared memory

EngineCore Process (Scheduler):
  On EVERY completed request → _get_routed_experts():
    reconstruct slot_mapping from KV block_ids (numpy)
    fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX)                 ← blocking file lock
    data = shm[slot_mapping].copy()      ← read from shared memory
  Attach to EngineCoreOutput → IPC → APIServer
```

**Problems:**
1. **Always-on overhead**: Both paths run unconditionally for all requests, even when no client needs routing data
2. **GPU→CPU sync on Worker hot path**: `slot_mapping.cpu()` and `device_buffer.cpu()` force CUDA synchronization every step
3. **Blocking I/O in event loop**: `fcntl.flock` + numpy memcpy in the Scheduler's single-threaded loop
4. **Shared memory as IPC**: Introduces a separate data channel (shm + flock) parallel to the existing `ModelRunnerOutput` → EngineCore IPC pipeline


### Proposed design: per-request opt-in with ModelRunnerOutput handoff

The root problem is architectural: routed experts data flows through a dedicated shared-memory channel with file locks, separate from the existing Worker → EngineCore IPC pipeline. This introduces GPU→CPU synchronization, blocking I/O, and cross-process locking on every forward step — regardless of whether any client needs the data.

The fix is to treat routed experts like any other Worker-produced side data (`pooler_output`, `kv_connector_output`): flow it through `ModelRunnerOutput`, gated on per-request opt-in.

#### API surface

Clients opt in per-request via `vllm_xargs`:

```python
POST /v1/completions
{
    "prompt": [...],
    "max_tokens": 1,
    "vllm_xargs": {"return_routed_experts": true}
}
```

The server-wide `--enable-return-routed-experts` flag remains, but only controls whether the `RoutedExpertsCapturer` is initialized (device buffer allocated, `capture_fn` bound to routers). It no longer implies always-on capture/save/read on every step.

#### Data flow

```
Worker Process:
  1. capture_fn() writes topk_ids to device_buffer during MoE forward (always, in CUDA graph)
  2. IF batch contains opted-in request:
     a. Extract routing deltas from device_buffer for this step's tokens
     b. Attach to ModelRunnerOutput.routed_expert_deltas: dict[str, np.ndarray]
        (req_id → ndarray of shape (num_new_tokens, num_layers, topk))
     GPU→CPU copy uses a separate CUDA stream (non_blocking=True) — does not sync the main stream

EngineCore (Scheduler):
  3. update_from_output(): for opted-in requests, append delta to request-local accumulator
     (one list.append per step — O(1), no numpy, no shm, no lock)

57378.title: [Bugfix][Platform] Fall back to torch when device-level NVML memory is unsupported (GB10)
57378.body:
## Problem

`nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo` is not implemented on integrated parts. On GB10 (DGX Spark) it raises
`NVMLError_NotSupported`, and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total` returns `[N/A]`. The platform
still resolves to `NvmlCudaPlatform` (`is_integrated_gpu()` is `True`), so
`get_device_total_memory()` propagates that error.

The visible damage is in `EngineArgs.get_batch_defaults()`, which wraps the call in
`try/except Exception` and falls back to `device_memory = 0`. A 121.7 GiB card therefore misses the
`>= 70 GiB` branch and lands on the smallest defaults, with nothing logged.

On this machine, before:

```
card reports (torch)                    121.7 GiB
current_platform.get_device_total_memory()  -> NVMLError_NotSupported
resolved max_num_batched_tokens  API=2048   LLM=8192
resolved max_num_seqs            API=256
```

after:

```
current_platform.get_device_total_memory()  -> 130669424640 (121.7 GiB)
resolved max_num_batched_tokens  API=8192   LLM=16384
resolved max_num_seqs            API=1024
```

So every DGX Spark is currently serving with batch defaults 4x lower than the ladder intends.

There is a second caller, `startup_plan.py:66`, which is *not* wrapped — with
`VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1` the same `NVMLError_NotSupported` aborts worker startup outright. That
path is opt-in (default `0`), which is why this shows up as quiet misconfiguration rather than a
crash for most users.

## Fix

Catch `NVMLError` and fall back to `torch.cuda.get_device_properties().total_memory` — the same
source `NonNvmlCudaPlatform.get_device_total_memory` already uses, and the same NVML-tolerance
shape as `is_fully_connected()` a few lines below. The discrete-GPU path is unchanged; the fallback
only runs when NVML refuses.

## Test

Verified on the affected hardware (NVIDIA GB10, compute capability 12.1, driver 580.95.05,
aarch64 / CUDA 13); the fallback value matches `torch`'s `total_memory` exactly.

I have not run this on a discrete NVIDIA GPU — I do not have one to hand — but that path is
untouched. No unit test here since it would be all pynvml mocking for a six-line guard; happy to add
one if you'd prefer it.

53726.title: Silent CUDA IMA (exit 0) in hybrid GDN + MTP k=3 + async scheduling on RTX 3090; persists through #50021/#45100/#53613-class fixes
53726.body:
### Title

Silent CUDA illegal-memory-access (exit 0) in hybrid GDN + MTP k=3 + async scheduling on RTX 3090 — persists through #50021/#45100/#53613-class fixes

### Environment

- vLLM 0.27.1 (pinned vendor tree; syv-ai/qwen38-27b-rtx3090 patch set incl. #50021-equivalent GDN bounds hardening, verified applied)
- GPU: RTX 3090 (sm86), driver 595.71.05, CUDA 13.x runtime via wheel
- Model: Qwen3.5-family **hybrid GDN** 27B, W4A16 (compressed-tensors/Marlin), native MTP head
- Serving config: `--speculative-config {"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"} --async-scheduling --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --max-num-seqs 4` (+ `--kv-cache-memory` pin), FlashInfer attention, PIECEWISE cudagraphs
- Reproduces on plain upstream-style config; no vendor attention kernels in the path

### Failure

Under mixed traffic (small requests completing while a long-generation request is mid-decode), the engine dies with:

```
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

surfacing at `CommonAttentionMetadata.seq_lens_cpu` (`gdn_attn.py build()` path), asynchronously reported. The API server then exits **with status 0** — under systemd `Restart=on-failure` the unit stays down silently.

Observed across 5+ crashes: the dying request is always mid-MTP-decode with `num_computed_tokens` ≈ 23.6K–26.2K and growing output (~400–3400 tokens), on prompts of ~22–46K tokens. Same `num_computed_tokens=23615` recorded twice on different prompts, suggesting a structural boundary rather than data dependence.

### What we already ruled out

All of the following are present in our tree and the crash still reproduces stochastically (~30–50% of heavy boots):

- #50021-equivalent bounds hardening on `i_t = num_accepted - 1` and mamba block-table columns (syv vendored copy, `_check_applied` verifies)
- #45100 (merged) — async non-align CPU accepted-count skip + `batch_size = m.num_reqs` in GDN metadata builder
- Partial #51599-consumer-side isolation for align mode
- A local backport of #53613's `num_accepted_tokens_event.synchronize()` inside `synchronize_input_prep()`

Also not it: async-scheduling toggle (crashes with it off too), k∈{1,2} vs k=3 (greens were small-sample noise), canary concurrency (not required), OOM (distinct signature, excluded by pinning KV pool and matching env exactly).

`CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` makes the run survive (race hidden). compute-sanitizer cannot reach the crash region within practical time on this workload.

### Minimal reproducer shape

1. Serve the model with the flags above at 131072 context.
2. Request A: ~22K-token prompt, short generation (completes).
3. Request B: ~22K-token prompt, `max_tokens≥3500`, tools schema attached, temp 0.6 — decode crosses the ~23.6K computed boundary.
4. Run repeated boots; expect IMA → EngineDeadError → exit 0 within 1–2 heavy requests roughly every other boot.

Driver available; happy to attach full logs/dumps (scheduler dumps captured via `dump_input.py` show the dying request each time).

### Ask

Guidance on which subsystem to instrument next (FlashInfer plan/workspace staleness under PIECEWISE replay? draft-slot padding path per gotcha that "every decode step is padded to num_speculative_tokens"? GDN recurrent-state page arithmetic at block boundaries?), or whether a known main-branch fix beyond the PRs above covers this signature.

Adding to @DONGRYEOLLEE1's `pidfd_getfd(2)` note — it also bites on **bare metal**, not just under a Docker seccomp profile, and here's the mechanism plus two fixes that don't need a vLLM change.

**Bare-metal cause:** `pidfd_getfd()` requires the same permission as `PTRACE_MODE_ATTACH`. Under the Yama LSM with `/proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope = 1` (the default on Ubuntu and most distros), that only succeeds between a process and its **direct child** without `CAP_SYS_PTRACE`. The PLE offload worker isn't a ptrace-eligible child of whichever process calls `pidfd_getfd()` on it, so the call returns `EPERM` — silently, late, after graph capture, no upfront hint. Same end symptom as the seccomp case, different gate.

**Two fixes, neither a code change:**

1. `sudo sysctl kernel.yama.ptrace_scope=0` (or edit the `/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf` that sets it, then reload) — host-wide.
2. `setcap cap_sys_ptrace+ep` on the venv's `python3`, or run the launcher under `sudo` — scoped, leaves the host policy intact.

**The offload worker's CUDA context is invisible to the memory profile, so the engine over-commits the GPU.**

Single RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120, 96 GiB), TP=1, `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=1`, `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, MTP k=3, `--max-model-len 81920`. Eight concurrent ~24k-token summarization requests at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.97`:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 320.00 MiB.
GPU 0 has a total capacity of 94.97 GiB of which 129.44 MiB is free.
Including non-PyTorch memory, this process has 94.12 GiB memory in use.
Process 726 has 730.00 MiB memory in use.'
```

Process 726 is this PR's PLE offload worker. It spawns after the engine takes its init snapshot, and it holds its own CUDA context of roughly 730 MiB that the profile never counts, so at 0.97 there is not enough real headroom for peak activation under concurrency. 1. **The utilization budget is wrong by the size of the worker's context.** Users set 0.95 to 0.97 on a 96 GiB card because that is normally safe, and here it is not.
